answer: A real person moves continuously, so a day of location fixes must form an unbroken chain with plausible speeds and no gaps that hide teleportation, smooth as velvet over a long road. A trace that vanishes from one valley and reappears on a distant island minutes later fails the envelope, a bridge crossed slowly passes, and a juniper grove beside the road allows tunnels but not miracles, so scripting hundreds of believable days grows costly.
